sources.entry: ClearDisk - Visualize and clean developer caches to quickly reclaim disk space. [![Open-Source Software][OSS Icon]](https://github.com/bysiber/cleardisk) ![Freeware][Freeware Icon]
ClearDisk - Visualize and clean developer caches to reclaim disk space on macOS.

summary.one_liner: ClearDisk is a free, open-source macOS menu bar app that scans known developer cache directories (Xcode, npm, Homebrew, Docker, pip, Cargo, Gradle and more) and moves selected ones to Trash.
summary.what_it_does: It scans 79 specific developer cache paths and shows their sizes with a plain-English description and a Safe/Caution/Risky level for each. It also has a project artifact scanner that finds stale per-project folders such as node_modules, .venv, build outputs and Unity/Unreal/Godot caches across 23 project types. A menu bar monitor shows disk usage with color thresholds at 80% and 90%, and it sends alerts at those levels. Storage forecasting uses a linear regression over 90 days of history to estimate when the disk will fill. Cleaning moves files to Trash rather than deleting them, and the app tracks bytes moved to Trash separately from space actually reclaimed after Trash is emptied. Updates are checked against GitHub Releases through Sparkle.
use_cases: Reclaim disk space taken by Xcode DerivedData and simulators
Clean npm, pnpm, pip, Cargo, Go and Gradle caches
Find old node_modules and .venv folders in project directories
Monitor disk usage from the macOS menu bar
Forecast when a Mac's disk will become full
Remove Docker and Homebrew caches safely via Trash
notable: Scans 79 known developer cache paths plus project artifacts in 23 project types
Risk levels (Safe, Caution, Risky) and descriptions for each cache
Moves files to Trash first and tracks space actually reclaimed after Trash is emptied
Menu bar disk monitor with storage forecast from 90-day usage history
No telemetry; network access limited to signed update checks
caveats: Building from source needs Xcode Command Line Tools and produces an ad-hoc signed app
Homebrew install requires an extra 'brew trust' step for third-party taps
